key_insight: Zatom-2 is a single generative atomistic foundation model that unifies molecules, materials, and proteins through large-scale multitask pretraining.
engineering_relevance: It offers a reusable pretraining stack for chemistry and materials design tasks, improving generation quality, force-aware control, and low-data transfer to biology-relevant protein design.
method: Pretrained on ~5 million atomistic structures from OMol25 and OMat24
Uses a multiscale Transformer with conditional flow matching
Supports generation, structure prediction, and energy/force prediction with force conditioning
evidence_signal: The model is evaluated on molecule and material generation benchmarks and reports improved molecular fidelity over Zatom-1, plus protein backbone designability rising from 67.8% to 74.8% after finetuning on 2,000 protein domains.
watch_item: Because the model combines multiple domains and objectives, performance may depend on careful dataset balancing and transfer settings, especially for low-data biological applications.
paper_title: Zatom-2: Multitask Pretraining on Atomistic Data for Generative Modeling across Domains
